`110-118`: ** Trivial** · **Functional Correctness** · **Quick win** **Assert `dimensions` on every batch request in the batching test.** The batching test checks only the input length of each request. It does not check `dimensions`. A change that drops `dimensions` from batches after the first would still pass the suite. **Reject empty input in `createEmbeddings` before the batch loop.** With `input: []`, the new loop makes no request and returns `embeddings: []` with zero usage. Before this change, the API rejected the empty array with a 400 error. Throw before the loop so an empty input reports an error, as the OpenAI endpoint and sibling activities do.
Suggested fix
```diff const texts = requireTextOnlyEmbeddingInput(options.input, this.name, model) + if (texts.length === 0) { + throw new Error(`${this.name} embed() requires at least one input`) + } ```

**Partition embedding requests by total token count as well as input count.** Each request holds at most 2048 inputs. The endpoint also rejects a request whose inputs total more than 300,000 tokens. The slice at `embedding.ts:97` does not check the token total. A 2048-input slice of long texts can therefore fail, even when smaller slices would succeed. This failure is not a regression from the PR. Requests of 2048 or fewer inputs keep the same single request, so the token limit already applied to them before the change. The PR fixes only the input-count limit for larger arrays. Splitting by token total needs a per-text token count, which the current code does not compute.
